name: DocuMind — Document Intelligence RAG System
tagline: Upload any document and ask questions — production RAG pipeline with exact page citations
purpose: A document intelligence system that lets users upload PDFs, Word documents, or text files and ask natural language questions. Returns answers with exact page citations from the source document.
problem_solved: Reading and extracting information from large documents (legal contracts, research papers, technical manuals) is time-consuming. DocuMind enables instant question-answering with source citations.

pipeline: ChromaDB Vector Storage (persistent collection per document)
LLM Response Generation (grounded answer with citations)
architecture.description: Classic RAG pipeline with ChromaDB as vector store. Documents are chunked at paragraph level, embedded, and stored with page metadata. Queries retrieve top-k semantically similar chunks, which are passed to the LLM as grounded context. Response includes exact page citations from source document.
key_design_choices: Semantic chunking (paragraph-level) over fixed-size chunking for better context preservation
ChromaDB for persistent, queryable vector collections
Citation tracking in chunk metadata for page-level attribution
Grounded responses — LLM cannot answer outside retrieved context

key_achievements: Semantic chunking with paragraph-level context preservation
Exact page citation tracking in every response
Support for PDF, DOCX, and TXT document formats
Persistent ChromaDB collections (documents survive server restart)
Grounded responses — LLM cannot hallucinate outside source document

engineering_decisions.decision: Why semantic chunking over fixed-size chunking?
engineering_decisions.reason: Fixed-size chunking (e.g., 512 tokens) splits mid-sentence, losing context. Semantic chunking splits at paragraph/section boundaries, preserving logical units of information. This significantly improves retrieval relevance.

ChromaDB provides a document-oriented vector store with built-in collection management — perfect for per-document collections. pgvector requires PostgreSQL setup and manual schema design. ChromaDB is faster to set up for a document QA use case.

Users need to verify AI answers against source documents, especially for legal or research use cases. Page citations enable trust and verification. Every chunk stored in ChromaDB includes page_number metadata for citation retrieval.

challenges: Scanned PDF extraction quality — handled with OCR fallback using Tesseract
Large document chunking strategy — solved with recursive text splitter with overlap
Multi-document query disambiguation — solved with collection-per-document isolation
